summary:
Florida stands under the United States national framework and adds a state layer a trans visitor meets directly on the ground, most sharply in public facilities. Under the Facility Requirements Based on Sex Act (Fla. Stat. 553.865), in force since 1 July 2023, a trans person may not use a restroom or changing facility consistent with their gender identity in buildings owned or leased by the state or local government: state offices, courthouses, legislative offices, prisons and jails, local immigration detention facilities, state parks, toll-road plazas, state schools, state universities, beaches and airports. The statute purports to cover all schools, public and private. Private businesses are outside its scope.

The statute's mechanics put the decision with an authority figure on site. Gender labels are required, an internal disciplinary procedure applies, and an authority figure may order a person to depart; a non-member who does not leave can be charged with criminal trespass. The ACLU of Florida advises that refusing to leave a sex-segregated restroom or changing facility can amount to criminal trespass and that each situation calls for fact-specific judgment and legal counsel.

There is one documented arrest. Marcy Rheintgen, a 20-year-old trans college student, was charged on 19 March 2025 after police, alerted in advance, arrested her washing her hands in a women's restroom at the Florida State Capitol, where she had declared "I am here to break the law" on entering. The misdemeanor trespass charge carried up to 60 days in jail and was described as the first arrest under Florida's transgender bathroom restrictions. On 20 June 2025 Leon County Judge Lashawn Riggans threw the case out: as a defendant charged under the statute she had no standing to argue that the law itself was illegitimate, so the statute was never substantively tested. No later arrest under the law is documented in this record.

The restriction reaches higher education through administrative rulings. On 23 August 2023 the Board of Education approved firing employees of 28 public community and state colleges who enter the forbidden bathroom, and on 18 October 2023 it voted to apply a similar restriction to private college and university buildings including student housing, with compliance proof due by 1 April 2024. The federal appellate rule moved the other way first: an August 2020 Eleventh Circuit ruling that a Ponte Vedra Beach high school violated the law by refusing a transgender student consistent restroom use was reversed in January 2023 when the court sided with the district to uphold the ban, which was codified on 17 May 2023.

State identity documents diverge from what many visitors hold. In January 2024 the Department of Highway Services and Motor Vehicles stopped issuing any driver's licence bearing a gender marker different from sex assigned at birth, treating holders, users and applicants as criminally guilty of fraud, with suspension and revocation of the document. In July 2024 transgender people born in Florida could not update or change sex on birth certificates despite explicit legislation permitting it. Before that closure, an amended birth certificate required an application to amend a Florida birth record, a notarized affidavit and a physician letter confirming appropriate clinical treatment, without requiring surgery or sterilisation; after 2011 a driver's licence or ID name change required a court order alongside a physician statement.

Gender-affirming care is restricted in state law, and the restrictions reach adults as well as minors. On 31 October 2022 the Medical Board required a 24-hour waiting period for adults before sexual reassignment surgery; on 4 November 2022 it approved a ban on gender-affirming healthcare for minors, effective 16 March 2023 and codified 17 May 2023, which prohibits hormone replacement therapy for transgender minors and adds adult barriers including a bar on insurance coverage and a requirement that treatment be administered by a physician rather than a nurse practitioner. Minors under 18 cannot receive puberty blockers, hormone therapy or confirming surgeries unless intersex, and a board memo stated that social transition should not be a treatment option. Senate Bill 254's Physicians Only provision prohibited nurse practitioners and physician assistants from providing gender-affirming care to transgender adults, which the Human Rights Campaign reported disrupted care for an estimated 80 percent or more of transgender clinic patients, with temporary or permanent suspensions after signing. A May 2023 law allows medical practitioners to refuse treatment on grounds of conscience, religion or belief. Litigation has partly checked these rules: three plaintiffs obtained a preliminary injunction on 6 June 2023 limited to themselves, the Eleventh Circuit stayed it on 26 August 2024, and a federal judge permanently blocked provisions banning care for minors and adults in June 2024.

Protection machinery at state level is thin. Florida's statutes do not address discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing or other areas, and nursing home and hospital protections in force since 2000, amended in 2007, cover sexual orientation but not gender identity. The state hate-crime law provides harsher penalties for crimes based on sexual orientation but does not cover gender identity. Since February 2021 the Florida Commission on Human Relations has announced enforcement of Bostock v. Clayton County (15 June 2020) to investigate employment, housing and public accommodations claims. Counties and cities comprising about 55 percent of the population, among them Jacksonville, Miami, Tampa, Orlando, St. Petersburg, Tallahassee and West Palm Beach, prohibit discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in private and public employment, housing and public accommodations.

Two advocacy organisations have warned travellers directly. On 12 April 2023 Equality Florida took what it called the unprecedented step of issuing a travel advisory on risks to the health, safety and freedom of those considering short or long-term travel or relocation to Florida, citing laws hostile to LGBTQ people alongside reproductive-health restrictions, gun-safety rollbacks and book bans and curriculum censorship; the organisation reports events and conferences cancelling. The Human Rights Campaign joined with an updated Florida travel advisory in May 2023, citing recently signed legislation, stopping short of a boycott. Same-sex marriage has been legal in Florida since 6 January 2015, when Brenner v. Scott held the state's ban unconstitutional.
tangentialFactors:
Florida's facility law is not isolated. At least 14 states have adopted laws barring trans women from women's bathrooms at schools and some government buildings, and the Equality Florida advisory places Florida's statutes within a wider set of measures on reproductive health, guns and school curricula that the organisation treats as travel-relevant for reasons beyond LGBTQ policy.

The state's approach to trans participation in sport predates the facility statute. A law of 1 June 2021 excluded transgender girls and women, defined as students of the male sex based on sex assigned at birth, from female school sports. In early 2023 the Florida High School Athletics Association recommended that female athletes supply menstrual cycle information to a school-accessible database, a measure speculated to serve both abortion-enforcement and detection of trans women. The Attorney General threatened competitions including an Irish step dancing competition and Miss America for allowing transgender competitors, describing them as deceptive and as depriving women of fair competition.

The Human Rights Campaign's description of the facility statute covers publicly owned or leased airports, government buildings, convention centres, parks, school campuses and stadiums, and imposes criminal penalties on visitors and residents alike who refuse to leave when asked, which is the wording a traveller is most likely to encounter.
localsOnly:
Resident-facing exposure extends to custody and to public funding. Senate Bill 254 of 17 May 2023 allows child custody modification on the basis that a child received or might receive gender-affirming care, and legislation of April 2023 allowed modifying or nullifying out-of-state parental custody agreements where the child is allowed or threatened with access, described by opponents as permitting removal of a child across state lines; protests against the measures included trans children being detained and one arrested for disturbing the peace.

Local protections exist but stop at the state line in force. Conversion therapy is banned in a number of cities, mainly in the Miami metropolitan area, and those bans have been struck down by the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals. In September 2023 Lake Worth Beach became an official LGBTQ sanctuary city. Nine counties, thirty cities and one town offer domestic partnership benefits. The Department of Agriculture added sexual orientation to its workplace policy in January 2019.

Two further statutes bear on public life. A May 2023 law bans adult live performances anywhere a minor might view them under criminal penalty, which Governor DeSantis said was about drag shows; it was preliminarily enjoined on 23 June 2023 as not all drag is obscene. HB 1001/SB 1134, passed 23 April 2026 and effective January 2027, prohibits state and local funding of or promotion for diversity, equity and inclusion as defined to include gender identity, with lawsuits and removal of officials as remedies; it has been interpreted as barring government support for LGBTQ organisations and events, illustrated by Palm Beach County denying a HUD grant to repair one LGBTQ organisation's headquarters air conditioning.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Florida's facility statute would survive a direct constitutional challenge is unresolved in this inventory. The single prosecution was dismissed on standing grounds on 20 June 2025, so the statute was never substantively tested, and no later prosecution is documented here.

The current appellate status of the gender-affirming care provisions is unresolved. The inventory records a preliminary injunction of 6 June 2023 limited to three plaintiffs, a stay by the Eleventh Circuit on 26 August 2024, and a federal judge permanently blocking provisions banning care for minors and adults in June 2024, without documenting what happened on appeal after that.

Whether the January 2024 driver's licence marker rule or the July 2024 birth certificate practice has been litigated is not sourced here. The inventory also does not document how the facility statute is applied at Florida airports in practice, nor any screening or document check specific to Florida ports of entry; those layers sit with the national record.

The Equality Florida travel advisory is dated 12 April 2023 and the Human Rights Campaign's update May 2023. No later reissuance or withdrawal by either organisation appears in this inventory, so their current status is unresolved.
